title: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: RDS (Hyaline Membrane Disease)
AAP surfactant / antenatal-steroid guidance (2020); ACOG/SMFM antenatal corticosteroids

changelog.change: Initial entry — surfactant-deficiency pathophysiology, risk factors, the clinical/radiographic picture, and prevention + treatment (antenatal steroids, CPAP-first, surfactant).

purpose: Surfactant-deficiency respiratory distress, almost exclusively in preterm infants. Antenatal corticosteroids for anticipated preterm delivery are the highest-yield preventive step; support the airway with CPAP first, rescue with surfactant.

body.text: Surfactant synthesis begins ~24–28 weeks; mature levels are generally reached after ~35 weeks. Without it, alveolar surface tension is high → progressive atelectasis, low compliance, rising work of breathing. Leading cause of neonatal respiratory morbidity and mortality.

items: Prematurity — the dominant risk factor; incidence rises sharply as gestational age falls.
Infant of a diabetic mother — hyperinsulinaemia delays surfactant maturation.
Caesarean delivery without labour — reduced endogenous cortisol surge.

Clinical: tachypnoea, nasal flaring, grunting, intercostal / subcostal retractions, cyanosis in room air, diminished breath sounds with fine crackles — onset within minutes to hours of birth, worsening over the first 24–48 h.
CXR: diffuse fine reticulogranular ('ground-glass') pattern with air bronchograms; severe → near-complete opacification ('white-out').

Antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone or dexamethasone) for anticipated preterm delivery — generally 24–34 weeks, and considered for late preterm 34–36⁺⁶ (ACOG/SMFM). Accelerates fetal lung maturity.

Respiratory support: CPAP first for a spontaneously breathing preterm infant; mechanical ventilation as needed, targeting lung-protective settings (low tidal volume, adequate PEEP, permissive gas-exchange targets).

Exogenous surfactant: for established RDS on escalating support — via ETT, or a less-invasive technique (LISA / MIST) or INSURE (INtubate–SURfactant–Extubate to CPAP) in a spontaneously breathing infant.
Supportive: thermoneutral environment, judicious fluids, treat a haemodynamically significant PDA, screen for the differential (TTN, pneumonia / sepsis, pneumothorax, congenital anomaly).

body.text: Complications of RDS and its treatment: air leak (pneumothorax, pulmonary interstitial emphysema), PDA, intraventricular haemorrhage, and — with prolonged oxygen / ventilation — bronchopulmonary dysplasia and retinopathy of prematurity.
